Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. ### Prerequisites

- [x] I have read the [dotnetup documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/tree/release/dnup/documentation/general/dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup issues](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3AArea-dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup discussions](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/discussions/categories/dotnetup).

### Issue type

Bug report

### Description

The block dotnetup writes to profile.ps1 runs `dotnetup.exe env script` on every PowerShell start and pipes it through Out-String and Invoke-Expression. The output is always the same two lines.

Numbers from my machine (Windows, pwsh 7.6, median of 21 fresh `pwsh -NoProfile` runs, timing only the block)

| Variant | Time |
|---|---|
| Block as shipped | ~400-700 ms |
| `dotnetup env script` alone | ~290 ms |
| Same with DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 | ~100 ms |
| Static `$env:` lines guarded by `Test-Path` | ~85 ms |
| Static `$env:` lines guarded by `[IO.File]::Exists` | ~12 ms |

Telemetry is set up before the command is known, so `env script` pays the full OpenTelemetry setup even though its flush is already cut to 10 ms. `Test-Path`, `Out-String` and `Invoke-Expression` each trigger module autoload in a new session. bash, zsh and fish pay the process and telemetry cost too.

I'll send three small PRs that can be taken independently. One switches the pwsh block to `[IO.File]::Exists` and a scriptblock. One skips telemetry for `env script`. One writes the env lines straight into the profile block and relies on `env set` to re-sync.

I'll send three small PRs that can be taken independently. One switches the pwsh block to `[IO.File]::Exists` and a scriptblock. One skips telemetry for `env script`. One writes the env lines straight into the profile block and relies on `env set` to re-sync.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

```sh
Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
```

Additional information:

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: IDE0005 not reported for an unused using of a namespace with C# 14 extension blocks when the file calls any extension method
Issues.Body:
**Version used:** .NET SDK 10.0.113

**Steps to reproduce:**

```xml
<!-- Lib.csproj -->
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <NoWarn>CS1591</NoWarn>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

```ini
# .editorconfig
root = true
[*.cs]
dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0005.severity = warning
```

```csharp
// Extensions.cs
namespace Lib.Ext;

public static class GuidExtensions
{
    extension(System.Guid id)
    {
        public bool IsEmpty => id == System.Guid.Empty;
    }
}

// User.cs
using Lib.Ext; // unused

namespace Lib;

public static class User
{
    public static int Go(string[] values) => values.Count();
}
```

`dotnet build`

**Expected:** IDE0005 on `using Lib.Ext;`.

**Actual:** no diagnostic (0 warnings). IDE0005 is reported when:
- `Go` makes no extension-method call (e.g. `values.Length`), or
- `GuidExtensions` uses a classic `public static bool IsEmpty(this Guid id)` instead of an extension block.

It looks like extension-member lookup marks every imported namespace that holds an extension block as used, even when nothing in it applies to the receiver or matches the name. Similar to #76974, for extension blocks.

Issues.Title: Skip BenchmarkDotNet weaving in design-time builds
Issues.Body:
Set `BenchmarkDotNetShouldWeaveAssemblies` to `false` in `Directory.Build.targets` when `DesignTimeBuild` is `true`.

BenchmarkDotNet's assembly weaver runs after `CoreCompile` and expects the compiled assembly to exist in `obj`. Because design-time builds do not emit the compiled assembly to disk, running the weaver during design-time builds fails. Disabling assembly weaving during design-time builds prevents these failures.

Issues.Title: Partition large test assemblies in single-machine RunTests runs
Issues.Body:
Single-machine (non-Helix) RunTests runs execute one process per test assembly. A handful of large assemblies (CSharp.Features, CodeStyle, Emit, Emit3, Semantic, LanguageServer.Protocol, RazorExtension) dominate the end of the run, leaving only one or two processes busy for the last ~15 minutes on the 4-core CI agents.

## Changes

- `--partition[:<path>]` (new RunTests option, opt-in) reads `eng/config/test-partitions.json` (or a custom file) and:
  - splits configured .NET Core assemblies into one process per group of class/namespace prefixes plus a remainder process (`FullyQualifiedName!~...`) so every test, including newly added ones, runs exactly once;
  - starts work items longest estimated duration first.
  - Partitioning is skipped for desktop assemblies, `--sequential`, `--testfilter`, and assemblies with `doNotPartitionReason` (wait-bound ones like Workspaces.MSBuild and LanguageServer).
- `eng/rebalance-test-partitions.cs` regenerates the config from the latest `Test Windows CoreClr Debug Single Machine` test durations in pipeline 95.
- `.github/skills/rebalance-test-partitions` documents the periodic refresh (intended to run every two weeks via an automation).
- The single-machine CoreClr jobs in `azure-pipelines.yml` pass `--partition`.

## Measurement (draft only)

The last commit (`TEMPORARY: ...`) runs the Windows single-machine job in PR builds and adds unpartitioned twins (`*_NoPartition`) for Windows and Linux so the same build gives an A/B comparison. It will be reverted before this is marked ready.

Local run pinned to 4 CPUs: 88.7 min baseline → 82.0 min with partitioning (86.0 min with longest-first ordering alone). 

CI results ("Run Unit Tests"/"Test" step, minutes; partitioned vs `_NoPartition` twin in the same build):

| Run | Build | Windows part. | Windows no-part. | Linux part. | Linux no-part. | Linux Spanish part. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1690583 | 74.5 | 74.2 (Emit failure) | 65.8 | 64.5 | 66.0 |
| 2 | 1690907 | 73.5* | 78.4 | 64.0 | 65.3 | 65.9 |
| 3 | 1691161 | 74.9 | 77.4 | 67.1 | 65.5 | 67.5 |
| **avg** | | **74.3** | **76.7** | **65.6** | **65.1** | **66.5** |

\* 85/86 items finished at 73.5 min; the unsplit `LanguageServer.UnitTests` then hung until the 120 min job timeout.

Net: Windows about -2.4 min (~3%), Linux no gain. Well short of the local estimate.

Why: partitioning does remove the 12-17 min tail (the last items now finish within seconds), but total process time rises ~10-16% (Windows run 1: 384 -> 446 process-minutes). On the 4-core agents running 6 processes the run is throughput-bound, so the extra work cancels most of the tail savings. The overhead is almost entirely in the IDE assemblies; the compiler ones split for free:

| LanguageServer.Protocol | 34.3 / 39.1 | 27.0 / 31.1 |
| RazorExtension | 20.8 / 29.4 | 14.8 / 15.5 |

Issues.Title: Limit Razor fallback discovery to affected types
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When a component falls back, its shell can leave dependent components with incomplete tag-helper metadata. #86451 addresses that by discovering all source types against the augmented compilation.

Collect dependency facts during fast discovery and rediscover only fallback components and affected component types. Route source candidates for non-component producers through the augmented compilation when a fallback exists, since their attributes and members can also depend on a shell. Keep descriptor and dependency comparisons separate so unchanged facts do not invalidate downstream work.

Fixes #84646.

## Performance

In-process BenchmarkDotNet runs on a synthetic project with 100 components, one fallback, and 100 MVC candidates:

| Edit | Merged fix | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unrelated component declaration | 14.8-17.8 ms | 20.7-24.5 ms |
| Fallback declaration | 33.3-36.1 ms | 29.3 ms |

These are separate, noisy runs; timings also varied in the no-fallback scenario. The additional dependency walk can cost several milliseconds on declaration edits, while changing the fallback declaration benefits from rediscovering fewer components. Real-solution profiling would help establish the practical trade-off.

The changed-file whitespace formatter reports the same three pre-existing diagnostics in `RazorSourceGeneratorTagHelperTests.cs` as on main.

Issues.Title: dotnetup: write env lines into the shell profile instead of running env script
Issues.Body:
Contributes to #57261.

The managed profile block ran `dotnetup env script` on every shell start, for all shells. Its output only depends on things `env set` already controls (which parts to wire, the install path, where dotnetup lives), so this writes those lines straight into the block. They're still guarded by the existing check that dotnetup is there, so the block does nothing if dotnetup is removed.

New pwsh block

```powershell
# dotnetup: begin
if ([System.IO.File]::Exists('C:\Users\me\.dotnetup\dotnetup.exe'))
{
    $env:DOTNET_ROOT = 'C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\dotnetup\dotnet'
    $env:PATH = 'C:\Users\me\.dotnetup' + [IO.Path]::PathSeparator + 'C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\dotnetup\dotnet' + [IO.Path]::PathSeparator + $env:PATH
}
# dotnetup: end
```

bash/zsh/fish get the same treatment with their own syntax. The lines come from the providers' `GenerateEnvScript`, so the block and `env script` can't drift apart.

Timing just the block in a fresh `pwsh -NoProfile` (median of 21-31 runs) went from 400-700 ms to about 8 ms.

Things worth a look
- The block has to be rewritten when the paths change. `env set` and `init` already do that, and a bare `env set` re-syncs.
- Existing blocks that call `env script` keep working. Users get the new block the next time `env set` or `init` runs. I didn't add a rewrite on self-update.
- The block now always has the full install path, even for the default location. Before, the default path was left out so `env script` could work it out at startup. The dotnetup path was already absolute, so the block was never really portable across machines.
- `DOTNET_DOTNETUP_DATA_DIR` is now read when the block is written, not at shell start.

I ran the generated pwsh block in pwsh 7.6 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 (including a path with a quote and a missing exe), and the bash one in Git Bash. 1320 dotnetup tests pass locally, excluding the E2E/network ones.

This overlaps with #57262 in the pwsh guard. Whichever goes second will need a small rebase.

Issues.Title: dotnetup: skip telemetry for env script
Issues.Body:
Contributes to #57261.

`env script` runs from the shell profile on every shell start. Telemetry gets built in `Main` before the command is known, so even with the 10 ms shell-startup flush budget it still pays for the whole OpenTelemetry and Azure Monitor setup. This checks the raw args for `env script` or `print-env-script` up front and turns telemetry off for that process. It doesn't go through the parser there because that would build the command tree before the UI language is set.

From a running pwsh, median of 21 runs of `env script --shell pwsh --dotnet --dotnetup`

| | default | DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 |
|---|---|---|
| before | 142 ms | 100 ms |
| after | 85 ms | 85 ms |

Earlier cold-start numbers on the issue showed a bigger gap (about 240 ms vs 80 ms).

The trade-off is that failures in `env script`, like an unsupported shell, won't show up in telemetry anymore. It also won't show the first-run notice, which is better for shell startup anyway.

The drain E2E test was using `env script` to get blobs on disk without a detached drainer racing it. It now runs `--help` with a new test hook that skips the drainer.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "dotnetup: skip telemetry for env script" (#57263)

Issues.Title: dotnetup: avoid slow cmdlets in the PowerShell profile block
Issues.Body:
Contributes to #57261.

The pwsh profile block used `Test-Path`, `Out-String` and `Invoke-Expression`. In a new session each of these loads a module on first use, and that happens on every PowerShell start. This switches to `[System.IO.File]::Exists` and dot-sources a scriptblock. The script is still joined and run as one unit, like the Out-String version did.

Timing just the block in a fresh `pwsh -NoProfile` (median of 41 runs, telemetry off so the exe cost stays small)

| | Time |
|---|---|
| `Test-Path` | 75 ms |
| `[IO.File]::Exists` | 6 ms |
| Out-String + Invoke-Expression | 177 ms |
| `-join` + dot-sourced scriptblock | 95 ms |

So roughly 145 ms less per shell start. I checked the new block in pwsh 7.6 and Windows PowerShell 5.1, and with the exe missing.

The paste-once activation command still uses Invoke-Expression since it isn't on the startup path.

Issues.Title: dotnetup PowerShell profile block adds ~0.5 s to every shell startup
Issues.Body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have read the [dotnetup documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/tree/release/dnup/documentation/general/dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup issues](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3AArea-dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup discussions](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/discussions/categories/dotnetup).

### Issue type

Bug report

### Description

The block dotnetup writes to profile.ps1 runs `dotnetup.exe env script` on every PowerShell start and pipes it through Out-String and Invoke-Expression. The output is always the same two lines.

Numbers from my machine (Windows, pwsh 7.6, median of 21 fresh `pwsh -NoProfile` runs, timing only the block)

| Variant | Time |
|---|---|
| Block as shipped | ~400-700 ms |
| `dotnetup env script` alone | ~290 ms |
| Same with DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 | ~100 ms |
| Static `$env:` lines guarded by `Test-Path` | ~85 ms |
| Static `$env:` lines guarded by `[IO.File]::Exists` | ~12 ms |

Telemetry is set up before the command is known, so `env script` pays the full OpenTelemetry setup even though its flush is already cut to 10 ms. `Test-Path`, `Out-String` and `Invoke-Expression` each trigger module autoload in a new session. bash, zsh and fish pay the process and telemetry cost too.

I'll send three small PRs that can be taken independently. One switches the pwsh block to `[IO.File]::Exists` and a scriptblock. One skips telemetry for `env script`. One writes the env lines straight into the profile block and relies on `env set` to re-sync.

### dotnetup version

0.3.0-preview.1.26554.3+a98e2d0757a9

Issues.Title: AffectedTests: make the 128 MiB test-map limit configurable (or split the map)
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to #55574 and #55405.

### Summary
`Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.AffectedTests` (18.14.0-preview.26569.4, .NET SDK 11.0.100) refuses to write a test map larger than a fixed 134217728 bytes:

    Affected-test mapping content exceeds 134217728 bytes.

The limit applies per test module and cannot be changed: there is no command-line option, environment variable or key in the `affected-tests-configuration-v1` config for it.

### Impact
A single xUnit v3 test project with ~12,000 tests over a large production assembly produces a map of about 350 MB, so affected-test selection cannot be used for it at all. A smaller project in the same solution (~2,900 tests, 86 MB map) works well: it runs 768 of 2,910 tests.

The only workaround is splitting the test project, a large structural change made only to fit the tool's limit. testfx itself excludes modules over the limit from collection (`docs/affected-test-selection.md`, `eng/collection-module-pool.ps1`).

### Repro
1. A test project with ~12k tests covering a large assembly.
2. `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLE_AFFECTED_TESTS=1 dotnet test --collect-test-map`
3. The collection fails with the message above.

### Ask
Any of:
- a configurable limit (option, environment variable or config key);
- a higher default;
- the map split into several files per module.

### Environment
.NET SDK 11.0.100 · Microsoft.Testing.Platform 3.0 preview · xUnit v3 · Windows 11

@Evangelink

Issues.Title: CA2241 false-positive diagnostic when using Composite [StringSyntax] on an extension method overload with a IFormatProvider parameter.
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

([I had originally posted this to `dotnet/roslyn-analyzers` in Feburary 2026](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/issues/7800), however that repo was recently archived, with instructions saying that issues concerning `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers` should be posted to `dotnet/sdk`, and issues with all other analyzers posted to `dotnet/roslyn`. I mention this because the CA2241 warning does originate from `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers` so this issue does belong in this repo, but I noticed all other GitHub issues concerning `[StringSyntax]` [are still being posted to `dotnet/roslyn`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues?q=is%3Aissue+StringSyntaxAttribute)).

--------------------

When using `[StringSyntax( StringSyntax.CompositeFormat )]` for a `String`-extension method overload with an `IFormatProvider` parameter, the CA2241 warning will be raised incorrectly, because the analyzer treats `IFormatProvider provider` as a composite-formatting parameter (like `Object? arg0` and `params Object[] args`) when it should not.


### Steps to reproduce

### Repro.cs:

```
global using StrSyn = global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.StringSyntaxAttribute;

using System;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

public class Program
{
	public static void Main()
	{
		// OK:
		String outWithoutFormatProvider = @"Arg0: {0}, Arg1: {1}, Arg2: {2}".Fmt( "arg0", 1, 2.0 );

		// CA2241 False-positive
		String outWithFormatProvider    = @"Arg0: {0}, Arg1: {1}, Arg2: {2}".Fmt( CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, "arg0", 1, 2.0 );
	}
}

public static class StringFormatExtensions
{
	const MethodImplOptions _Inline = MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining | MethodImplOptions.AggressiveOptimization;

	#region Fmt (With IFormatProvider parameter)

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object)"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String Fmt( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, IFormatProvider? formatProvider, Object? arg0 ) =>  String.Format( formatProvider, format, arg0 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object, Object)"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String Fmt( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, IFormatProvider? formatProvider, Object? arg0, Object? arg1 ) =>  String.Format( formatProvider, format, arg0, arg1 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object, Object, Object)"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String Fmt( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, IFormatProvider? formatProvider, Object? arg0, Object? arg1, Object? arg2 ) =>  String.Format( formatProvider, format, arg0, arg1, arg2 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object[])"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String Fmt( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, IFormatProvider? formatProvider, params Object?[]? args ) =>  String.Format( formatProvider, format, args: args ?? Array.Empty<Object?>() );

	#endregion

	#region Fmt (No IFormatProvider parameter)

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object)"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.CurrentCulture"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String Fmt( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, Object? arg0 ) =>  String.Format( CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, format, arg0 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object, Object)"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.CurrentCulture"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String Fmt( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, Object? arg0, Object? arg1 ) =>  String.Format( CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, format, arg0, arg1 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object, Object, Object)"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.CurrentCulture"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String Fmt( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, Object? arg0, Object? arg1, Object? arg2 ) =>  String.Format( CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, format, arg0, arg1, arg2 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object[])"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.CurrentCulture"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String Fmt( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, params Object?[]? args ) =>  String.Format( CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, format, args: args ?? Array.Empty<Object?>() );

	#endregion

	#region FmtInv (No IFormatProvider parameter)

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object)"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.InvariantCulture"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String FmtInv( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, Object? arg0 ) =>  String.Format( CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, format, arg0 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object, Object)"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.InvariantCulture"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String FmtInv( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, Object? arg0, Object? arg1 ) =>  String.Format( CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, format, arg0, arg1 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object, Object, Object)"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.InvariantCulture"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String FmtInv( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, Object? arg0, Object? arg1, Object? arg2 ) =>  String.Format( CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, format, arg0, arg1, arg2 );

	/// <summary>Calls <see cref="String.Format(IFormatProvider, String, Object[])"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.InvariantCulture"/>.</summary>
	[MethodImpl( _Inline )]
	public static String FmtInv( [StrSyn( StrSyn.CompositeFormat )] this String format, params Object?[]? args ) =>  String.Format( CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, format, args: args ?? Array.Empty<Object?>() );

	#endregion
}

```



### Expected behavior

With any Composite Formatting extension-method then the analyzer should check if any call-site arguments correspond to any `IFormatProvider provider` parameters, and if so, should not treat them as composite-formatting arguments (especially if the other parameters have names like `arg0...argnN` or are `params Object?[] args` parameters).

### Actual behavior

A CA2241 diagnostic is raised for this expression ( `@"Arg0: {0}, Arg1: {1}, Arg2: {2}".Fmt( CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, "arg0", 1, 2.0 );`  ) because it thinks `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` is the first of 4 composite-formatting arguments, but the call-site actually has only 3 composite-formatting arguments.


### Is this a regression?

No. This behaviour has been consistent since CA2241 was introduced.

### Are there any workarounds?

No.

(In practice I either suppress the diagnostic at the call-site with `#pragma warning disable CA2241`; In other projects I ended-up removing the `[StringSyntax]` attribute from all of the methods which accept an `IFormatProvider`, but using either option means losing compile-time verification of composite-formatting args.

Issues.Title: [wasm] Require the browser workload for CoreCLR native items
Issues.Body:
Ports the workload requirement from dotnet/runtime#137716 into the SDK's copy of the Mono toolchain workload manifest, which is the copy the SDK ships.

On CoreCLR browser, `NativeFileReference`, `NativeLibrary`, `DirectPInvoke` and `DirectPInvokeList` items are linked or bound through a native relink, so they need the wasm-tools workload. Without it, build and publish succeed with at most a warning, and the P/Invokes throw `DllNotFoundException` at runtime.

`_WasmNativeWorkloadNeeded` can't see items, because it is computed in the property pass. Instead, for CoreCLR browser projects with these items when the workload isn't otherwise in use, this adds a `MissingWorkloadPack` item for `Microsoft.NET.Runtime.WebAssembly.Sdk.${NetVersion}`, the same item the workload resolver adds for property-driven requirements. The SDK then fails the build with NETSDK1147. The item is added in two places:
- During evaluation, so Visual Studio and `dotnet workload restore` suggest wasm-tools through `GetSuggestedWorkloads`, which checks its condition before any BeforeTargets run.
- From a target before `_CheckForMissingWorkload` and `GetSuggestedWorkloads`, for items from `Directory.Build.targets` or package targets, which are imported after the workload manifest.

MSBuild evaluates a target's condition before running its BeforeTargets, so `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.ImportWorkloads.targets` now checks `@(MissingWorkloadPack)` on the `ShowMissingWorkloads` tasks instead of on those two targets. A new `WorkloadTests` case checks that a target-added `MissingWorkloadPack` reaches `GetSuggestedWorkloads`. It fails with the old conditions.

Mono is unchanged and keeps the `NativeFileReference` warning.

Validation, in dotnet/runtime against the runtime copy of this file with the same change:
- The no-workload WBT `NativeItemsRequireWorkload` covers `DirectPInvoke` in the project file and in `Directory.Build.targets`, `NativeFileReference` in the project file, and `NativeLibrary` in `Directory.Build.targets`.
  - Every case fails the build with "the following workloads must be installed: wasm-tools".
  - For the project-file cases, `GetSuggestedWorkloads` returns wasm-tools.
- Each half alone misses a case:
  - With only the evaluation-time item, the `Directory.Build.targets` case builds successfully.
  - With only the target, `GetSuggestedWorkloads` returns nothing.
- No-workload `WorkloadRequiredTests` passed (56), with `NativeRef_RequiresWorkload` now expecting NETSDK1147 on CoreCLR.
- With the workload installed, these still pass: `NativeLibraryTests` (7), `NativeFileReferenceTriggersRelinking`, and the `DirectPInvoke*` WBTs (5).

In this repo, `WorkloadTests` passed (15). The wasm manifest change was not tested here.

Kept as a draft until dotnet/runtime#137716 merges.

> This PR description was generated with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: Track additional ReadyToRun compiler outputs for incremental builds
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`_CreateR2RImages` currently lists only `OutputR2RImage` and `OutputPDBImage` as outputs. A composite compilation also writes one rewritten component file per input (PE/Mach-O component assemblies, or `.wasm` component stubs). If one of those files is deleted or becomes stale, the target is still considered up to date. Publish then fails, or it copies an outdated component.

This PR adds an `AdditionalOutputs` metadata contract to `_ReadyToRunCompileList`:

- `AdditionalOutputs` is a semicolon-separated list of files the compiler produces besides `OutputR2RImage` and `OutputPDBImage`. `_CreateR2RImages` now uses `Outputs="%(OutputR2RImage);%(OutputPDBImage);%(AdditionalOutputs)"`. Batching splits the list, so incrementality stays per entry: deleting or aging a single extra output recompiles only that entry.
- `PrepareForReadyToRunCompilation` fills it in for the composite entry from the same component paths it already uses to build `ReadyToRunFilesToPublish`, so the outputs and the published files come from one source of truth.
- **Extension point:** targets that change which files crossgen2 emits, typically through extra compiler arguments, can update the metadata after `_PrepareForReadyToRunCompilation`. Planned crossgen2 output-layout changes then only need a metadata update in the task or in the extending targets, not a new target or a workaround. For example:

```xml
<_ReadyToRunCompileList Update="@(_ReadyToRunCompileList)" Condition="'%(CreateCompositeImage)' == 'true'"
                        AdditionalOutputs="$(_MyBundlePath)" />
```

## Motivation

dotnet/runtime#137713 makes crossgen2 bundle composite WebCIL components into a single `<app>.components.wasm` file for browser CoreCLR. That file was not a tracked output, so the runtime targets temporarily deleted the composite owner image to force a recompile when the bundle was missing. That workaround has now been removed; this PR models the extra output directly. The review comment at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/137713#discussion_r4646044683 asked for the output to be modeled properly in the SDK instead.

## Merge sequencing

1. **This PR (dotnet/sdk).** The change is additive. Existing targets that do not set the metadata behave as before, while composite publishes also track their component files.
2. **dotnet/runtime.** Port the same task and target change to `src/tasks/Crossgen2Tasks`, which must stay equivalent to the SDK copy, and set `AdditionalOutputs` to the bundle path in `Browser.CoreCLR.targets`. Remove the owner-image invalidation workaround. These runtime changes do not need to wait for the SDK version to flow into runtime's `global.json`: the in-tree path uses the shim.
3. **SDK flow.** Once the updated SDK reaches runtime's pinned SDK version, the explicit stock-SDK test path will also honor `AdditionalOutputs`. Until then, that opt-in path will not rebuild solely because a bundle is missing; the bundle has not shipped, so this temporary gap is accepted. Do not retain or restore the owner-deletion workaround for this transition.

No capability flag is needed. Older SDKs ignore `AdditionalOutputs`; newer SDKs use it for incremental tracking.

## Validation

- `./build.sh`: succeeded.
- `./.dotnet/dotnet scripts/RunTests.cs -- --project test/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~GivenAPrepareForReadyToRunCompilation"`: passed, 5/5. This includes new `AdditionalOutputs` assertions for Mach-O and wasm composite planning.
- `./.dotnet/dotnet scripts/RunTests.cs -- --project test/Microsoft.NET.Publish.Tests/Microsoft.NET.Publish.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~It_recompiles_composite_image_when_a_component_output_is_missing|FullyQualifiedName~It_recompiles_readytorun_images_when_crossgen2_arguments_change|FullyQualifiedName~It_can_publish_readytorun_composite_with_subdirectory_relative_path"`: passed, 3/3. The new test deletes a composite component and confirms the next publish recompiles it.

The suite ran before a final cleanup that removed only an unused private property; it was not re-run after that change. The new publish test has not been confirmed to fail without the target change.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description was drafted with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.1xx] Fix race in dotnet-watch RunsWithIterationEnvVariable test
Issues.Body:
Fixes a flaky `dotnet-watch.Tests` failure that is blocking the VMR backflow PR #57185 into `release/10.0.1xx`.

## Failure

`LaunchSettingsTests.RunsWithIterationEnvVariable` failed on #57185 (Helix job `72e39f31-da98-40eb-8e24-8c408fedd04c`, `dotnet-watch.Tests.dll.4`):

```
Expected text not found in the output:
DOTNET_WATCH_ITERATION = 2
```

The test log already contains `DOTNET_WATCH_ITERATION = 2`, but it arrived after the assertion ran.

## Root cause

The test waits for dotnet-watch's `Waiting for a file to change` message, which goes to stderr, and then synchronously calls `AssertOutputContains` on the app's stdout line. `AwaitableProcess` reads the two streams independently, so the app's line can arrive after the watch message.

## Fix

Use `await App.WaitUntilOutputContains(...)`, which `main` and `release/10.0.4xx` already use (introduced in #51727). This is a test-only change.

Related: #57209 (satellite-assembly UTF-8 test) and #57237 (BrowserTests races) fix the other test failures blocking `release/10.0.1xx` CI.

Issues.Title: Improve code-review skill with checks that human maintainers often make
Issues.Body:
## Summary

With this change, the `code-review` skill finds more of the problems that human maintainers find, and it does not add wrong findings on correct code.

In an eval on 18 old dotnet/sdk PRs, the skill found the problem that the human reviewer found in **78% of reviews, up from 70%**. On 6 control PRs with correct code, the new rules never fired wrongly.

Problems that the old skill missed, and the new skill now finds:

| Problem | Example | Before | After |
| --- | --- | :-: | :-: |
| A bool option accepts a value that is then ignored | #26963 | 0/3 | 3/3 |
| Telemetry sends TFMs without a hash | #27042 | 0/3 | 2/3 |
| A CLI error message tells the user to use Visual Studio | #28811 | 0/3 | 2/3 |

What changed in the skill:

- **A checklist of problems that human maintainers often find.** I read 1,530 review comments from @tmat, @baronfel, and @dsplaisted. Each of the 12 checklist items links to example PRs.
- **Shorter text.** I removed repeated text and filler. No rule is removed.
- **Clearer severity.** Formatting and leftover code are never ❌ errors.

## Eval

I used [Vally](https://aka.ms/vally) to compare the skill on `main` (before) with the skill in this PR (after). Agent: claude-sonnet-5.5. Judge: gpt-6.1-terra. 3 trials for each case. The agent could not use GitHub, so it could not read the original review comments.

There are three kinds of cases. Each case is the diff of a real dotnet/sdk PR or commit:

- **11 PRs that the checklist cites.** A human reviewer found a real problem. The judge checks whether the review finds the same problem.
- **7 other PRs.** The same, but the checklist does not cite them.
- **6 controls.** Merged code that uses a pattern correctly, where a broad checklist rule could fire by mistake. For example, `AcceptOnlyFromAmong` instead of an enum, or a message that sends users to the Visual Studio Installer for a workload that Visual Studio owns. The judge fails the review if it makes that wrong claim.

A second judge checks every ❌ error in every review. It fails the review if any ❌ error is wrong, speculative, or only style.

| Result | Before | After |
| --- | :-: | :-: |
| Found the problem, PRs that the checklist cites | 19/32 (59%) | 24/33 (73%) |
| Found the problem, other PRs | 18/21 (86%) | 18/21 (86%) |
| Found the problem, all PRs | 37/53 (70%) | 42/54 (78%) |
| Controls: no wrong claim | 17/18 (94%) | 18/18 (100%) |
| Reviews with no wrong ❌ error, when the skill loaded | 23/54 (43%) | 34/71 (48%) |
| ❌ errors per review, when the skill loaded | 1.6 | 1.6 |
| Skill loaded | 54/71 (76%) | 71/72 (99%) |

What this shows:

- The new skill finds more of the problems that the checklist describes. On the other PRs, it finds the same number.
- The new rules did not fire wrongly on correct code. The old skill once said that `--self-contained` must not accept `true` or `false`.
- When the skill loads, both versions give the same number of ❌ errors, and about the same number of wrong ones.
- With either version, about half of the reviews have at least one ❌ error that the judge rejects. This PR does not cause that problem, and it does not fix it.
- Some cited cases got worse: #26427, #43393, and #16530 each lost 1 trial. Results change between runs. In earlier runs, these cases were the same or better.

Limits:

- 24 cases is a small sample, and one model judged all results.
- The eval compares the whole new skill with the whole old skill. It does not measure the checklist alone.
- Each case contains only the files that the PR changed. The reviewer cannot read callers or other code.
- One "before" trial failed because the model lookup timed out.

<details>

```js
// Creates a git repo with the base files committed and the PR change left uncommitted.
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { rmSync } from "node:fs";

const git = (...args) => execFileSync("git", args, { stdio: "inherit" });
git("init", "-q", "-b", "main");
git("config", "core.autocrlf", "false");
git("config", "user.name", "Eval");
git("config", "user.email", "eval@example.com");
git("add", "-A", "--", ".", ":!.eval");
git("commit", "-q", "-m", "Initial commit");
git("apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", ".eval/change.patch");
rmSync(".eval", { recursive: true, force: true });
```
