<details>
<summary>build.py</summary>

```python
"""Builds the vally eval for the dotnet/sdk code-review skill.

Each case is a historical dotnet/sdk PR where a human maintainer found a concrete
problem in a review comment. The fixture is the PR diff at the commit that the
reviewer saw (`.xlf` files removed), plus the merge-base version of each changed
file. setup.mjs commits the base files and leaves the diff uncommitted, so the
agent reviews "my uncommitted changes".

Usage: python build.py <path-to-sdk-repo> <variant>=<ref> [<variant>=<ref> ...]
Needs: gh (authenticated), git.
"""
import json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys

E = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO, VARIANTS = sys.argv[1], dict(a.split("=", 1) for a in sys.argv[2:])

# (pr, reviewer, text in the review comment, rubric)
CASES = [
 ("28059", "baronfel", 'Split("=", 2)', "The review reports that splitting the `-p`/`--property` `key=value` input on every `=` (for example `Split(\"=\")` in ReleasePropertyProjectLocator) breaks or truncates property values that themselves contain `=`, and that the split must happen only at the first `=`."),
  ("26427", "baronfel", "Target property should be hashed", "The review reports that the new `msbuild/build` telemetry event sends properties other than `ProjectPath` (for example `Target`) without hashing them, although they can contain user-defined values such as custom target names, and that these values must be hashed or filtered out."),
 ("27042", "baronfel", "hash each of these TFMs", "The review reports that the new `dotnet new` MSBuild-evaluation telemetry sends target framework (TFM) values unhashed, which is inconsistent with the existing MSBuild telemetry that hashes TFMs; the TFMs should be hashed."),
 ("26963", "baronfel", "ArgumentArity.Zero", "The review reports that the new boolean `--blame-crash-collect-always` (or a similar `--blame-*` flag) option accepts an explicit value such as `false` that is then silently ignored or discarded when forwarded, and that the flag should take no argument (for example `Arity = ArgumentArity.Zero`) so that an explicit value is a parse error."),
 ("26155", "baronfel", "string[]` form of `Parse`", "The review reports that the new in-process callbacks build a command line as one interpolated string (for example `$\"add {projectName} package {packageName}\"`) and parse it, which breaks for paths or values that contain spaces or quotes; they should pass a `string[]` of arguments to the parser instead."),
 ("29017", "baronfel", "define an enum", "The review reports that the new `--format` option is a free-form string and should instead be constrained to the allowed values (for example with an enum or `AcceptOnlyFromAmong`), so that System.CommandLine validates the input and shows the allowed values in help."),
 ("28811", "baronfel", "reference VS", "The review reports that the new CLI error message for a corrupt solution file refers to Visual Studio (tells the user to save the solution in VS), which is not appropriate for a CLI message; it should instead tell the user how to fix the file itself."),
 ("16530", "dsplaisted", "hard-code", "The review reports that a workload install test uses a try/catch with a forced-failure assertion (for example `true.Should().BeFalse()`) instead of `Assert.Throws`, or that test expectations are derived from the code under test instead of being hard-coded."),
 ("18815", "dsplaisted", "NETCoreAppMaximumVersion", "The review reports that the new `IsNetCoreAppTargetingLatestTFM` condition hard-codes the current .NET version, which must be updated for every major release; it should compare with `NETCoreAppMaximumVersion` (or an equivalent existing property) instead."),
 ("26369", "dsplaisted", "NuGetPackageNotFoundException", "The review reports that the new code in WorkloadManifestUpdater catches all exceptions (a broad `catch`) when it should catch only the expected `NuGetPackageNotFoundException`, so that other failures are not hidden."),
 ("43393", "tmat", "GetCustomAttributesData", "The review reports that the try/catch added in HotReloadAgent is too wide (it wraps the whole loop) and should wrap only the `GetCustomAttributesData()` call that can fail, so that bugs elsewhere in the loop are not hidden and keep a useful stack trace."),
]

# Other cases: no checklist item cites these PRs. 12085 was in the first run; the others were added after it.
OTHER = [
 ("12085", "dsplaisted", "duplicate", "The review reports that the LINQ `GroupBy`/`Where` query in CheckForDuplicateItemMetadata is lazy and is enumerated more than once, so the grouping work is done several times; it should be materialized once (for example with `ToList()`)."),
 ("35029", "tmat", "will be null here", "The review reports that dotnet-watch sets the launch-profile environment variable from `launchProfileName`, which is null when no profile is specified and the default profile is selected, so the variable is missing or wrong; it should use the name of the profile that was actually selected."),
 ("52683", "tmat", "excludes all directories that contain", "The review reports that the conversion of exclusion glob patterns to excluded directories in FilePathExclusions is incorrect: for example `**/a/**` should exclude the directories that match `**/a`, and patterns such as `*.*` (which does not match files without an extension), `**/*/*`, or `**/**` are not handled correctly."),
 ("18204", "dsplaisted", "checking if the string contains the manifest ID", "The review reports that the new manifest-directory filter uses a substring check (for example `Contains`) of the directory path or name against the outdated manifest IDs, so a manifest whose ID contains another ID is wrongly excluded; it should compare the manifest ID exactly."),
 ("13545", "dsplaisted", "net5.0-windows-windows", "The review reports that for a `net5.0` target framework with WPF or Windows Forms, the alias logic appends `-windows` to a value that can already contain it, which produces an incorrect TFM such as `net5.0-windows-windows`, or that the test uses `net5.0` where `net5.0-windows` is the valid value and so misses this bug."),
 ("28628", "dsplaisted", "can also be `WinExe`", "The review reports that the new RuntimeIdentifier inference condition compares `OutputType` with `Exe` and so misses `WinExe` applications; it should use `_IsExecutable` or `HasRuntimeOutput` instead."),
 ("18910", "dsplaisted", "also need to remove `TargetFramework`", "The review reports that when the workload-collection target calls referenced projects, it does not remove (undefine) the `TargetFramework` global property, so a multi-targeted project (for example `net6.0-ios;net6.0-android`) passes its TFM to a referenced project that does not target it; `TargetFramework` must be removed for those calls."),
]
# Controls: merged commits that use a pattern correctly. A broad checklist rule could
# flag them by mistake. The control grader fails if the review makes that wrong claim.
# (commit, wrong claim)
CONTROLS = [
 ("1b21906849", "that the `--format` option of `dotnet sln list` should use an enum instead of `AcceptOnlyFromAmong`, or that its values are not restricted"),
 ("ef02ba74a7", "that the new CLI message about workloads that Visual Studio installed must not refer to Visual Studio or the Visual Studio Installer"),
 ("93b4dfc3d8", "that the new test must not change project XML with `TestProject.ProjectChanges` and must use a different helper instead"),
 ("3e70852cf6", "that `--self-contained` must use `ArgumentArity.Zero` or must not accept an explicit `true` or `false` value"),
 ("ed75fed7a3", "that the validation of the workload set version that comes from `global.json` belongs in the parser or command definition instead of the command"),
 ("af6ecc2994", "as an error (❌) that the Roslyn compiler-cache telemetry properties (such as cache status, language, and timings) must be hashed because they contain user-defined or personal data"),
]

JUDGE = ("Judge only whether the agent's final review contains a finding that identifies the specific problem in the rubric. "
         "Paraphrase is acceptable, and the finding can have any severity. The finding must point at the relevant code and give the same mechanism; "
         "a vague or generic remark does not count. Ignore all other findings. "
         "Fail if the timeline shows that the agent read the upstream pull request or its review comments (GitHub web pages, `gh`, or the GitHub API).")

CONTROL = ("Pass unless the agent's final review claims {claim}. "
           "That claim is wrong for this code. Ignore the rubric above and all other findings. "
           "Fail if the timeline shows that the agent read the upstream pull request or its review comments.")

PRECISION = ("Check every finding marked ❌ (error) in the agent's final review. Ignore the rubric above. "
             "Pass if there are no ❌ findings, or if each ❌ finding is a real problem in the change that justifies blocking the merge. "
             "Fail if any ❌ finding is wrong (the code does not do what the finding says), is speculative without a concrete mechanism, "
             "or is only style, formatting, naming, wording, or a minor improvement. Use the repository snapshot to check the code.")

PROMPT = ("Review my uncommitted changes in this repository before I open a pull request. "
          "This is a partial checkout of dotnet/sdk: it contains only the files that my change touches. "
          "Do not use the network, GitHub, or `gh`; review only the local changes. Do not change any files. "
          "Give your findings in your final answer.")


def gh(*args, binary=False):
    out = subprocess.run(["gh", "api", *args], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    return out if binary else json.loads(out)


def build_case(pr, user, needle):
    comments = gh(f"repos/dotnet/sdk/pulls/{pr}/comments", "--paginate")
    c = next(c for c in comments
             if (c.get("user") or {}).get("login", "").lower() == user and needle.lower() in c["body"].lower())
    base, head = gh(f"repos/dotnet/sdk/pulls/{pr}")["base"]["sha"], c["original_commit_id"]
    merge_base = gh(f"repos/dotnet/sdk/compare/{base}...{head}")["merge_base_commit"]["sha"]
    diff = gh(f"repos/dotnet/sdk/compare/{base}...{head}", "-H", "Accept: application/vnd.github.diff", binary=True).decode()
    parts = [p for p in re.split(r"(?m)^(?=diff --git )", diff)
             if p.startswith("diff --git") and not re.match(r"diff --git a/\S+\.xlf ", p)]
    d = os.path.join(E, "cases", pr)
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "base"))
    open(os.path.join(d, "change.patch"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write("".join(parts))
    for p in parts:
        if "\nnew file mode" in p.split("@@")[0]:
            continue
        path = re.match(r"diff --git a/(\S+) ", p).group(1)
        blob = gh(f"repos/dotnet/sdk/contents/{path}?ref={merge_base}", "-H", "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw", binary=True)
        f = os.path.join(d, "base", *path.split("/"))
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(f), exist_ok=True)
        open(f, "wb").write(blob)
    json.dump(dict(pr=pr, user=user, path=c["path"], commit=head, merge_base=merge_base, comment=c["body"]),
              open(os.path.join(d, "meta.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1)


def build_commit_case(sha):
    """Fixture from a local commit: the parent's version of each changed file, plus the commit diff."""
    git = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, *a], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    parent = git("rev-parse", f"{sha}^").decode().strip()
    diff = git("diff", "--binary", parent, sha, "--", ".", ":!*.xlf").decode()
    d = os.path.join(E, "cases", sha)
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "base"))
    open(os.path.join(d, "change.patch"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(diff)
    for p in re.split(r"(?m)^(?=diff --git )", diff):
        if not p.startswith("diff --git") or "\nnew file mode" in p.split("@@")[0]:
            continue
        path = re.match(r"diff --git a/(\S+) ", p).group(1)
        f = os.path.join(d, "base", *path.split("/"))
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(f), exist_ok=True)
        open(f, "wb").write(git("show", f"{parent}:{path}"))


def write_skills():
    for variant, ref in VARIANTS.items():
        d = os.path.join(E, "skills", variant, "code-review")
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        text = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "show", f"{ref}:.github/skills/code-review/SKILL.md"],
                              capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
        open(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md"), "wb").write(text)


def common_graders():
    q = json.dumps
    return ["      - type: prompt", "        config:", "          scoring: binary", f"          prompt: {q(PRECISION)}",
            "          evidence: [trajectory, repo]",
            "          evidence_read_budget: { max_tool_calls: 30, max_total_chars: 200000 }",
            "      - type: skill-invocation", "        config:", "          required: [code-review]"]


def write_eval():
    q = json.dumps
    lines = ["name: sdk-code-review-human-findings",
             "description: Does the code-review skill find the problem that a human maintainer found in a historical dotnet/sdk PR?",
             "type: capability",
             "defaults:", "  timeout: 20m", "  judge_timeout: 5m", "  judge_model: gpt-6.1-terra", "  judge_reasoning_effort: high",
             "agent_environment:",
             "  env:",
             "    GH_TOKEN: eval-no-network",       # gh in the agent shell cannot read the upstream PR
             "    GITHUB_TOKEN: eval-no-network",   # Copilot itself uses COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN from the vally process
             "    GH_PROMPT_DISABLED: '1'",
             "  files:", "    - src: setup.mjs", "      dest: .eval/setup.mjs",
             "  commands:", "    - node .eval/setup.mjs",
             "stimuli:"]
    for set_name, cases in (("cited", CASES), ("other", OTHER)):
      for pr, user, _, rubric in cases:
        lines += [f"  - name: pr-{pr}",
                  f"    tags: {{ reviewer: {user}, case: '{pr}', set: {set_name} }}",
                  f"    prompt: {q(PROMPT)}",
                  "    agent_environment:",
                  "      files:",
                  f"        - src: cases/{pr}/base", "          dest: .",
                  f"        - src: cases/{pr}/change.patch", "          dest: .eval/change.patch",
                  "    rubric:", f"      - {q(rubric)}",
                  "    graders:",
                  "      - type: prompt", "        config:", "          scoring: binary", f"          prompt: {q(JUDGE)}"] + common_graders()
    for sha, claim in CONTROLS:
        lines += [f"  - name: ctl-{sha}",
                  f"    tags: {{ case: '{sha}', set: control }}",
                  f"    prompt: {q(PROMPT)}",
                  "    agent_environment:",
                  "      files:",
                  f"        - src: cases/{sha}/base", "          dest: .",
                  f"        - src: cases/{sha}/change.patch", "          dest: .eval/change.patch",
                  "    rubric:", f"      - {q('The review does not claim ' + claim + '.')}",
                  "    graders:",
                  "      - type: prompt", "        config:", "          scoring: binary", f"          prompt: {q(CONTROL.format(claim=claim))}"] + common_graders()
    lines += ["scoring:", "  weights:", "    prompt: 1.0", "    skill-invocation: 0.0", "  threshold: 1.0"]
    open(os.path.join(E, "eval.yaml"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for pr, user, needle, _ in CASES + OTHER:
        build_case(pr, user, needle)
        print("built", pr)
    for sha, _ in CONTROLS:
        build_commit_case(sha)
        print("built", sha)
    write_skills()
    write_eval()
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>analyze.py</summary>

```python
"""Summarizes a vally experiment run for the code-review skill eval.

Reports, per variant:
- recall: the review finds the human-reported problem (cited and other PRs),
- controls: the review does not make a known-wrong claim about correct code,
- precision: every ❌ finding is a real, blocking problem (all cases),
plus skill loading, finding counts, time, and a network-use check.

Usage: python analyze.py <experiment-output-dir>
"""
import collections, json, os, re, statistics, sys

R = sys.argv[1]
E = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
variants = [v for v in ("before", "after") if os.path.exists(os.path.join(R, v, "results.jsonl"))]
case_set = {}
for line in open(os.path.join(E, "eval.yaml"), encoding="utf-8"):
    m = re.search(r"case: '(\w+)', set: (\w+)", line)
    if m:
        case_set[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)

GRADER = {'prompt "Judge only': "found", 'prompt "Pass unless': "control", 'prompt "Check every': "precise", "skill-invocation": "loaded"}
NET = ("web_fetch", "web_search", "api.github.com", "github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull", "gh pr ", "gh api", "curl ", "Invoke-WebRequest")

trials = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(list))  # case -> variant -> [dict]
stats = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(list))
leaks = []
errors = []
errors = []
for v in variants:
    for line in open(os.path.join(R, v, "results.jsonl"), encoding="utf-8"):
        o = json.loads(line)
        if o.get("type") != "trial-result":
            continue
        if not o.get("gradeResult"):
            errors.append((v, o["stimulus"], o.get("status")))
            continue
        case = o["stimulus"].split("-", 1)[1]
        g = {}
        for d in o["gradeResult"]["details"]:
            for prefix, key in GRADER.items():
                if d["name"].startswith(prefix):
                    g[key] = d["passed"]
        trials[case][v].append(g)
        out = o["trajectory"].get("output") or ""
        stats[v]["findings"].append(len(re.findall(r"(?m)^\s*(?:#+\s*)?\**\d+[.)]\s", out)))
        stats[v]["errors"].append(out.count("❌"))
        stats[v]["seconds"].append(o["durationMs"] / 1000)
        for ev in o["trajectory"]["events"]:
            if ev.get("type", "").startswith("tool") and any(k in json.dumps(ev) for k in NET):
                leaks.append((v, case, o["trialIndex"]))


def count(sets, key, v):
    t = [g.get(key, False) for c in trials if case_set.get(c) in sets for g in trials[c][v]]
    return f"{sum(t)}/{len(t)} ({100 * sum(t) / max(1, len(t)):.0f}%)"


main_key = {"cited": "found", "other": "found", "control": "control"}
print("| Case | Set | " + " | ".join(variants) + " |")
print("| --- | --- | " + " | ".join(":-:" for _ in variants) + " |")
for c in sorted(trials, key=lambda c: (["cited", "other", "control"].index(case_set[c]), c)):
    k = main_key[case_set[c]]
    print(f"| {c} | {case_set[c]} | " + " | ".join(f"{sum(g.get(k, False) for g in trials[c][v])}/{len(trials[c][v])}" for v in variants) + " |")

print()
print("| Metric | " + " | ".join(variants) + " |")
print("| --- | " + " | ".join(":-:" for _ in variants) + " |")
rows = [("Found, PRs that the checklist cites", {"cited"}, "found"),
        ("Found, other PRs", {"other"}, "found"),
        ("Found, all PRs", {"cited", "other"}, "found"),
        ("Controls: no wrong claim", {"control"}, "control"),
        ("No wrong ❌ errors, all cases", {"cited", "other", "control"}, "precise"),
        ("Skill loaded", {"cited", "other", "control"}, "loaded")]
for label, sets, key in rows:
    print(f"| {label} | " + " | ".join(count(sets, key, v) for v in variants) + " |")
for key, label in (("findings", "Findings per review (mean)"), ("errors", "❌ per review (mean)"), ("seconds", "Seconds per review (mean)")):
    print(f"| {label} | " + " | ".join(f"{statistics.mean(stats[v][key]):.1f}" for v in variants) + " |")
print()
print(f"Tool calls that used the network or GitHub: {len(leaks)}", leaks[:5])
print(f"Trials without a grade (execution errors): {len(errors)}", errors[:5])
```

</details>

Issues.Title: [CI triage] TimeoutStartsWithFirstTestApplication times out waiting for cancellation on Windows FullFramework
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

#### Failure

A `dotnet test` policy unit test timed out waiting for the policy to signal cancellation after the first test application started. This prevents CI from verifying when the timeout begins.

### Steps to reproduce

See the [historical Windows FullFramework test result](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1690099&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=47177742&resultId=103809&paneView=debug). No local reproduction is known.

### Expected behavior

The policy does not time out before the first application starts, then signals `TestRunCancellationReason.Timeout` after the configured interval while an application is active.

### Actual behavior

`dotnet.Tests.CommandTests.Test.TestRunPolicyTests.TimeoutStartsWithFirstTestApplication` threw `System.TimeoutException: The operation has timed out.` at the test's wait for the cancellation signal. The exception is from the test wait, not evidence that the policy signaled a timeout.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown.

### Are there any workarounds?

None verified. The same build ID later had a successful pipeline check; the named test result on retry is unavailable.

### dotnet --info output

Unavailable.

### IDE version

N/A.

### Other details

#### Possible cause

The test uses a real timer, so a delayed timer callback is one possibility. The retained result cannot distinguish a delayed callback from failure to arm the timer or publish cancellation; the original logs and timeline were inaccessible. The neighboring tests already use a manual clock for deterministic policy checks, but replacing the real timer here without understanding the failure could hide a timer integration problem.

Issues.Title: [CI triage] PositiveResultIsCachedForSixHours fails its first classification assertion on Windows FullFramework
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

#### Failure

A CLI telemetry detector unit test failed in Windows FullFramework CI. Its first lookup returned a negative classification even though the test supplies a stub that returns a positive result.

### Steps to reproduce

See the [historical test result](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1684158&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=46994272&resultId=103928&paneView=debug). No local reproduction is known.

### Expected behavior

The first lookup reports the positive probe result, and the second lookup uses the cached result.

### Actual behavior

`InternalMicrosoftDetectorTests.PositiveResultIsCachedForSixHours` failed at the first positive-result assertion with `FluentAssertions.Execution.AssertionFailedException: Expected boolean to be True, but found False.` The test did not reach the cache assertions.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown.

### Are there any workarounds?

None verified. GitHub retains a later successful check for the same build ID, but the individual test result on retry was unavailable.

### dotnet --info output

Unavailable.

### IDE version

N/A.

### Other details

#### Possible cause

The test uses the detector's real probe-stage deadline, and the probe is started on the thread pool. Scheduling delay could cause the detector to reject the result, but the retained assertion does not report the detector outcome, and the original console and timeline were inaccessible. The evidence does not establish a cache defect or justify changing the deadline; the detector outcome and probe diagnostics would help distinguish the causes on recurrence.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Add contextual parallel test output (backport of #57236)
Issues.Body:
Backport of #57236 to release/11.0.2xx.

This is a manual SDK-only backport because the automatic cherry-pick conflicts across 34 files. It adapts the behavior to this branch's MTP 2.5 / MSTest 4.5 baseline instead of importing main-only prerequisites.

### Release-branch adaptations

- Contextual module output is enabled only for `TF_BUILD=true` with parallelism greater than one, and is excluded for help, discovery, and test-map collection.
- Failure and message lines include module identity; the SDK uses the evaluated module TFM because MTP 2.5 does not send handshake key 21.
- Azure Pipelines receives a grouped per-module recap. Module totals are omitted if execution or disposal fails, while aggregate exit codes remain intact.
- Live child output is drained for up to five seconds; truncation is reported. Child host output is prefixed without rewriting Azure or GitHub workflow commands.
- Coverage-summary, heartbeat-renderer, errored-assemblies, and progress-policy changes were omitted because their corresponding features are absent from this release branch. No TestFx sources, vendored-file manifests, or package versions were changed.

### Validation

- `.\build.cmd -bl /m:1` — succeeded with 0 errors. The full build reported 138 NuGet audit warnings (`NU1902` for `System.Text.Json` and `NU1903` for `Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler`); this backport does not change those package versions or audit settings.
- `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .github\skills\targeted-test\scripts\RunTargetedTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationActionQueueTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationLaunchTests|FullyQualifiedName~ProcessOutputCollectorTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests"` — 163 passed, 0 failed.
- `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .github\skills\targeted-test\scripts\RunTargetedTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~RunProjectWithMSTestMetaPackageAndMultipleTFMs_UsesContextualOutputOnlyInAzureWhenParallel"` — 1 passed, 0 failed. The composed test uses the release-pinned Microsoft.Testing.Platform `2.5.0-preview.26477.3` and MSTest `4.5.0-preview.26477.3` packages (TestFx commit `c670f66a454615d321aa8f67dc23cd9194c1d0ac`). It asserts Azure parallel failures return 2 with module context and a grouped recap; Azure serial and non-Azure parallel failures return 2 without contextual output; an Azure parallel passing/zero-test run returns 0 with a grouped recap.
- Red/green evidence: temporarily removing module-identity emission compiled successfully and caused two focused reporter tests to fail on the missing labels. After restoring the implementation, the focused suite passed.

### Known limitations

- MTP 2.5 does not provide handshake keys 21/22 or honor the child-host group opt-out. The SDK falls back to the evaluated TFM; host-supplied TFM metadata and in-progress test messages are unavailable on this branch. The release-pinned host emits Azure groups only when both `--report-azdo` and `--report-azdo-groups` are explicitly enabled; they are not enabled by default.
- Validation was performed on Windows; the hosted Azure DevOps UI was not inspected.

Issues.Title: Improve parallel test output in Azure Pipelines
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Attribute interleaved output from parallel Azure Pipelines test modules to their assembly and declared target framework, with contextual progress and centrally grouped summaries.
- Preserve workflow-command lines, existing exit codes and selection counts, and bound the wait for process-output streams before the final verdict.
- Negotiate optional test-progress support; older hosts retain module-only heartbeat.

The companion [microsoft/testfx#12549](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/pull/12549) changes are required for full progress and grouping behavior. Merge TestFx first, then this SDK change; flow aligned TestFx packages before downstream rollout. The reviewed packaged TestFx source is `8bbb93c41344ce34ab0516f9996cc96570fe2a0c`.

## Validation

- Windows x64 canonical shipping SDK: `.\build.cmd -bl` — passed, exit 0.
- Focused SDK tests: `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationLaunchTests|FullyQualifiedName~ProcessOutputCollectorTests|FullyQualifiedName~CoverageSummaryTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestCommandProgressPolicyTests|FullyQualifiedName~ParallelAzureRun_ReportsMergedCoverageInTheFinalGroupBeforeTheVerdict|FullyQualifiedName~ParallelCiRun_AttributesOutputAndKeepsTheFinalFailureVerdict|FullyQualifiedName~RunAffectedTestsWithoutTestHost_ReportsSelectionAndSummary|FullyQualifiedName~ParallelAffectedRun_ShowsSelectedOutModuleWithoutCountingItAsASkippedTest' --test-binlogs` — 375 passed, exit 0.
- Native-published tests: `.\test\dotnet-aot.Tests\run-aot-tests.ps1 -Trx -Filter 'FullyQualifiedName~CoverageSummaryTests'` — 41 passed, exit 0. Test-publish warnings concerned dump extensions and FluentAssertions AOT analysis.
- Composed shipping-SDK fixture: `$env:PARALLEL_FIXTURE_DIR='parallel-fixture5'; node '<sdk-session-files>\check-parallel.cjs' '<sdk-worktree>\artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet\dotnet.exe' 'preview5-final'` — exit 0. The clean fixture used Platform/AzureDevOpsReport `3.0.0-preview.26599.5`, MSTest `5.0.0-preview.26599.5`, and AffectedTests `18.13.0-preview.26563.2`. Native-default and forced-managed runs covered normal, framework skip, empty and mixed affected selection, fallback, failing test (exit 2), plain/ANSI output, actual Azure DevOps annotations, active/slow progress, and a held output pipe. `--report-azdo` takes the existing managed fallback. A 40-column ConPTY run exited 0.
- New SDK with `preview.26599.1` hosts succeeded with module-only heartbeat. Same-binary Ctrl+C controls exited 130 with no final recap in both contextual and non-contextual modes; cancellation lifecycle is unchanged.

`<sdk-session-files>` and `<sdk-worktree>` replace private absolute paths.

TestFx `.5` package SHA-256 values:

| Package | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| Microsoft.Testing.Platform | `62B2A73B2C9EA5180442344BE14D1DD9CB7C7299A06A014573BD49873ABB18C1` |
| Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.AzureDevOpsReport | `B653376612478B1DCA141626F4BBF08A0B6E183F1F72104A6F78349CE436E109` |
| MSTest | `C8A0C7EA92AF22F838C8023CDC95DB3A7B52D3D9485E14A7914B06C7CBE84DF4` |
| MSTest.Sdk | `953B44C40A1A1124EA289CFACF8ED307ED35A4AB4C7F579CE5DC5DCD5E2F3823` |
| MSTest.TestFramework | `3358BD86596F32F350164EF28BB2716F91F449F6EE59F515B18BDE8379E66771` |
| MSTest.TestAdapter | `0A68A5D13A55200CD67E1A6CCC77811588C2E72EBBE2820CF7B2A64F27E5EA36` |

Evidence and the composed fixture are retained locally in the session artifacts, not hosted in this PR. Validation was on Windows x64; the hosted Azure DevOps UI and other platforms were not exercised. Older hosts may still emit overlapping Azure DevOps groups.

## Review and test-value evidence

Multiple review/fix rounds addressed declared-TFM refinement, scoped coverage headings, command preservation, and ambiguous rejected-host/retry summary totals. Revision `097abea96562af8dbeef3ecc61886c465fa16f2e` passed 375 focused tests, 41 published NativeAOT tests, and the aligned composed cases. Follow-up review fixes in `2e54492a656c479d4b032d585401c6781544990d` (legacy-format tests pin `TF_BUILD=false`; grouped recap omits ambiguous module totals after execution or disposal failures; one write per module label; fake-clock contextual heartbeat tests) were rebuilt and passed 126 focused tests (`TerminalTestReporterTests` 101, `TestApplicationActionQueueTests` 13, `SilenceDrivenHeartbeatRendererTests` 7, globbing integration 5) and all 16 native/managed composed cases with expected exits (failure cases 2, others 0). The companion [TestFx decision record](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/8d0b2384942ef5ff8df6a490d76e177c9651632c/docs/decisions/parallel-test-output.md) records executed reporter mutations and real-wire red/green comparisons, including a capable peer receiving no progress before the fix and correctly identified progress afterward. Those targeted comparisons do not establish mutation coverage for every SDK path.

Issues.Title: Regression: Explicit configuration value overwritten by environment variable since .NET SDK 11
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

dotnet build/publish -p:Configuration=X is ignored when the ``CONFIGURATION`` environment variable is set. -c X works; SDK 10.0.404 works.

SDK | Command| Result
-- | -- | --
11.0.100 | -p:Configuration=Debug, env CONFIGURATION=Release | obj/Release ❌ (Expected Debug)
11.0.100 | -c Debug, env CONFIGURATION=Release | obj/Debug ✔
11.0.100 | -p:Configuration=Debug, без env | obj/Debug ✔
10.0.404 | -p:Configuration=Debug, env CONFIGURATION=Release | obj/Debug ✔



### Steps to reproduce

```
dotnet new classlib -f net10.0 -o repro
cd repro
$env:CONFIGURATION = 'Release' 
dotnet build -p:Configuration=Debug
```

### Expected behavior

Release notes states that an explicit command-line option still takes precedence, and empty or whitespace-only environment values are ignored. So -p:Configuration also should take precedence over environment variable.

### Actual behavior

Explicit -p:Configuration value overwritten by environment variable. 

### Is this a regression?

Yes. May also documented as breaking changes if this is desired сhanges. 

### Are there any workarounds?

Change p:Configuration=X to -c X to keep explicit configuration value X.

### dotnet --info output

```console
.NET SDK:
 Version:           11.0.100
 Commit:            297acf930f
 Workload version:  11.0.100-manifests.073a2387
 MSBuild version:   18.12.2-1.26529.118+297acf930

Runtime Environment:

 RID:         win-x64

```

Issues.Body:
`dotnet-new.IntegrationTests` timed out on macOS arm64 while running `AllCommonItemsCreate`, with the test host terminated after 48 minutes.

  - Partition `dotnet-new.IntegrationTests` by test class on macOS arm64.
  - Isolate resource-intensive template test classes instead of grouping up to 128 methods in one work item.

A previously closed SDK issue reported a different active test with a similar macOS arm64 hang pattern, but it does not establish recurrence of this exact failure.

## Error Details

Exact excerpt:

- **Work-item exit code:** `7`; test application exit code: `137`
- **Console:** [Helix console log](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/5633f8ca-330c-488f-9839-06a783b20822/workitems/dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.dll.1/files/console.9a5d23f2.log?api-version=2019-06-17)

The TRX sidecar recovered 26 results, with 25 executed and passed; the active test remained `AllCommonItemsCreate` when the dump was taken. No named assertion failure was established.

**Observed:** The `dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.dll.1` test host on the macOS arm64 queue remained in `AllCommonItemsCreate` until the 48-minute hang-dump threshold. Helix captured a dump, recovered streamed results, and the test application ended with exit code 137.

**Assessment:** The evidence establishes a test-host hang or non-graceful termination during this integration test, but does not establish why progress stopped. The generic downstream monitor failure, if present, would be a consequence rather than the cause; no artifact-download cascade is implicated by this observation.

**Confidence:** **Medium** for the observed hang and termination; **Low** for the underlying cause.

**Alternatives / Unknowns:** The dossier does not distinguish an SDK/template operation deadlock, process/resource termination, or an agent-level condition. It also does not establish a source-change trigger or recurrence.

## Suggested Investigation

1. Analyze `dotnet_2702_hang.dmp` and the console around `AllCommonItemsCreate` to identify the blocked thread and termination reason.
2. Compare the test and template-generation path on macOS arm64 with the last passing run, then rerun the focused test on the same queue to determine reproducibility.
3. If the dump indicates external termination rather than a managed wait, inspect Helix agent resource and health telemetry; otherwise trace the blocking SDK/template operation in the test and product source.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Test the in-repo TemplateEngine samples instead of the published package
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
Backports #57175 (originally part of #57089 on `main`) to `release/11.0.2xx`.

`TemplateEngineSamplesTest` installs the latest published `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Samples` package. The 11.0.100 package changed the F# sample to a plain SDK-style project, so the checked-in `sample06 --language F#` snapshot no longer matches and the test fails on every PR into this branch (for example #57231 and #57228). This change:

- copies the in-repo sample templates into the test output (`Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Samples.csproj` + a non-assembly `ProjectReference` from `dotnet-new.IntegrationTests`),
- installs the templates from that folder instead of nuget.org, and
- updates the F# snapshot to the in-repo sample content.

Relates to #57042.

**Validation:** conflict-free cherry-pick of the 11.0.1xx commit with an identical diff. The updated snapshot is byte-identical to the in-repo sample on this branch. The pending flow #57221, which contains this change on top of `release/11.0.2xx`, passes all 16 `TemplateEngineSamplesProjectTest` cases. Tests were not run locally.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Use stable feature band for build-number preview SDKs
Issues.Body:
## Summary

11.0.2xx preview builds being inserted into VS use the version label `preview` with no iteration number, e.g. `11.0.200-preview.26568.113`. Today `SdkFeatureBand` treats the second prerelease component as part of the band, so each build gets a unique, date-based band (`11.0.200-preview.26568`). As a result:

- `dotnet workload update` / `workload search version` find no workload sets ("No workload versions found for SDK feature band 11.0.200-preview.26568").
- Installing a workload set requires `--version` or a global.json `workloadVersion`.
- Install state is stored per band, so each new insertion loses any pinned workload set version.

## Change

When the first prerelease component is `preview` and the second is a numeric build number (>= 10000, which Arcade short-date build numbers always are), the version now maps to the **stable** feature band, the same way `dev`/`ci`/`rtm` builds already do.

| SDK version | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `11.0.200-preview.26568.113` | `11.0.200-preview.26568` | `11.0.200` |
| `11.0.200-preview.5.26568.113` | `11.0.200-preview.5` | `11.0.200-preview.5` (unchanged) |

Numbered previews keep their own separate workload sets.

## User-visible impact

- Build-number preview SDKs share workload sets, install state, and install records with stable SDKs in the same band (e.g. GA 11.0.200). They will pick up `Microsoft.NET.Workloads.11.0.200` by default.
- Until the first stable workload set for the band ships, there is no automatic fallback to 1xx workload sets; `--version` is still needed.
- Any state stored under the old `11.0.200-preview.<date>` folders is ignored.
- The resolver source is linked into the MSBuild SDK resolver, so VS and the SDK need to ship this change together.

## Testing

- Added `SdkFeatureBandTests` cases for SDK versions and workload set versions. These pass locally on net12.0 and net472.
- Manual testing against a daily 11.0.2xx build confirmed the current behavior: workload sets were not found without `--version`, and `--version 11.0.100.1` worked.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "[release/11.0.2xx] Use stable feature band for build-number preview SDKs" (#57239)

Issues.Title: Add regression tests for no-build single-file publish mismatches
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
## Summary

Test-only follow-up to #57111, which added `NETSDK1247` for `publish --no-build` when a single-file bundle input is missing. #57111 covered a deleted intermediate assembly and the supported publish-only `PublishSingleFile` host switch. It verified the mismatched build/publish sequences from #37367 by hand only. This PR adds automated regression tests for them. No product code changes.

Relates to #37367 and #57111.

## New tests (`GivenThatWeWantToPublishASingleFileApp`)

| Test | Sequence | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `It_reports_missing_inputs_on_no_build_publish_with_runtime_identifier_not_used_by_build` | Original #37367 recipe: `restore -r <rid>`; `build -c Release -p:PublishSingleFile=true` (no RID); `publish --no-build --no-restore -r <rid> -c Release -p:PublishSingleFile=true` | Exit 1, `NETSDK1247` for a file under `obj/Release/<tfm>/<rid>/`, no `MSB4018` |
| `It_reports_missing_inputs_on_no_build_publish_with_configuration_not_used_by_build` | Self-contained RID project: `build -c Release`; `publish --no-build -c Debug -p:PublishSingleFile=true` | Exit 1, `NETSDK1247` for a file under `obj/Debug/<tfm>/<rid>/`, no `MSB4018` |

Both tests use the real `dotnet restore/build/publish` CLI commands so that `--no-build`/`--no-restore` match the reported scenario.

The assertion checks the localized message prefix plus the RID/configuration-specific intermediate directory, not a specific file name. In both mismatches the first missing input reported is the single-file host (`apphost.exe` on Windows) rather than the app assembly. `_CreateSingleFileHost` is skipped when the intermediate assembly doesn't exist, and the host comes first in `FilesToBundle`. The message still points to the wrong-configuration/RID directory and gives the remedy. Reviewers may want to decide whether a follow-up should report the assembly first. This PR leaves the behavior unchanged.

## Validation

Ran against a freshly built redist SDK (`build.cmd`) with the repository test runner. The run covered the two new tests plus #57111's existing tests in the same class (`It_reports_missing_inputs_on_single_file_publish_with_no_build` ×4, `It_uses_appropriate_host_on_publish_with_no_build` ×2), sequentially (class-level parallelism): **8/8 passed** on win-x64.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add regression tests for no-build single-file publish mismatches" (#57238)

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.1xx] Fix ordering races in dotnet-watch BrowserTests
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
Relates to #57235

Backports the `BrowserTests.cs` changes from #52897 and #53498, and the `ApplyDeltaTests.cs` changes from #52897. These are on `main` and `release/10.0.4xx` but never reached `release/10.0.1xx`. This change only touches test code.

## Root cause

dotnet-watch writes its log messages to **stderr**, including `❌ ... error ENC0023` and `Restart is needed`. The `❔ Do you want to restart your app?` prompt, the app's output, and the test browser's `🧪 Received` lines go to **stdout**. `AwaitableProcess` merges both streams through two independent async readers, so the order between them isn't guaranteed.

`WaitForOutputLineContaining` takes lines off a single queue in arrival order. A line it takes while looking for something else can't satisfy a later wait. In the hang from #57235 (build 1690453, attempt 2), stdout delivered the restart prompt about 0.7s before the stderr `❌ ENC0023` line. The wait for the error line consumed the prompt, so the next wait for the prompt never matched. Meanwhile dotnet-watch sat at the prompt waiting for a key. The harness timeout (`HELIX_WORK_ITEM_TIMEOUT` minus 10s, about 1h) is longer than VSTest's 25-minute blame inactivity timeout, so blame killed the run first.

In attempt 1 of the same build, `BrowserDiagnostics` passed. The work item failed because `LaunchesBrowserOnStart` hit the same kind of race: it asserted on the stderr `Launching browser` line after waiting only for the stdout `Content root path:` line.

`ApplyDeltaTests` had the same exposure: it used ordered waits and asserted on output already received, across both streams.

## Changes

- `BrowserDiagnostics`: replace ordered `WaitForOutputLineContaining` calls with `WaitUntilOutputContains`, as in #52897.
- `LaunchesBrowserOnStart`: wait for each expected line instead of asserting on output already received, as in #53498. This keeps the release branch's two-argument `LaunchingBrowser.GetMessage` call.
- `ApplyDeltaTests` (separate commit): 161 calls now use `WaitUntilOutputContains`: 63 `WaitForOutputLineContaining`, 88 `AssertOutputContains`, and 10 `AssertOutputLineStartsWith`. It also adds #52897's four `ClearOutput()` calls, so later waits can't match stale lines. In `AutoRestartOnRuntimeRudeEdit`, #52897's four ordered waits for agent messages are kept; those lines all come from one stream, so their order is reliable. The changes are adapted to the messages and descriptors `release/10.0.1xx` emits (for example `HotReloadSucceeded` and `HotReloadChangeHandled` instead of `main`'s `ManagedCodeChangesApplied`/`StaticAssetsChangesApplied`).
  - Not included from #52897: un-skipping `ProjectChange_DirectoryBuildProps_Delete` (#49545) and its rewrite (it stays skipped and unchanged), the new MauiBlazor scoped-CSS steps, and a whitespace-only change.

## Validation

- Ran `build.cmd` on `release/10.0.1xx`.
- Ran `dotnet test test\dotnet-watch.Tests\dotnet-watch.Tests.csproj` locally on Windows, with TRX and binlog output:
  - `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.UnitTests.BrowserTests"`: 5/5 passed.
  - `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.UnitTests.ApplyDeltaTests"`: 30 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed. The 9 tests were already skipped on this branch, including `AutoRestartOnRuntimeRudeEdit`, `BlazorWasm`, `BlazorWasmHosted`, and `MauiBlazor`, so their edits are only compile-checked.

These runs show the tests still pass with the change. Passing runs can't prove the races are gone, since they only show up on some runs.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "[release/10.0.1xx] Fix ordering races in dotnet-watch BrowserTests" (#57237)

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118740 - Aspire Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118741 | ASP.NET Core Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. For the affected legacy prereleases, correct the generated handlers before using or deploying the generated application. #### Manual repair for generated Identity handlers This repair also applies to applications generated with the affected 11.0 scaffolding packages and Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet 10.0 RC versions above; it does not require migrating to a different scaffolding tool. In the generated `ForgotPassword` and `ResendEmailConfirmation` handlers, retain the existing user lookup, missing-user responses, password-reset confirmation checks, token generation and callback-URL encoding. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118741](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118741) ### Acknowledgements - [Leonardo Souza](https://www.linkedin.com/in/capleonardo-souza) with [Delfia](https://delfia.tech/) - Attila.Cs(zerodaybugs.com) with https://zerodaybugs.com/ ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

FileBufferingReadStream buffer allocation can allow unauthenticated multipart-form requests to exhaust memory. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70467 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-770 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The table lists the affected package range and the fixed NuGet version. ### ASP.NET Core 2.3 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities) | >= 2.3.0, <= 2.3.13 | 2.3.14 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check the application's Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities package reference against the affected range above, including transitive dependencies brought in by Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http. Use `dotnet list package --include-transitive` to inspect resolved dependencies. ### How do I fix the issue? Update each applicable package reference to its patched version listed above, then rebuild and redeploy the application. Updating only the installed runtime does not update an application's standalone package references. Applications referencing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http must resolve Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities to version 2.3.14 or later. Add or update a direct WebUtilities reference if necessary to override an older transitive dependency. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. An insecure temporary directory used by Aspire CLI-generated builds can allow a local attacker to influence MSBuild response-file discovery and execute code with the privileges of the developer running the CLI. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22101 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-379 (Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions) - **MSRC severity:** Important ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario concerns CLI-generated server and integration builds on non-Windows systems when a local attacker can influence automatic MSBuild response-file discovery through an attacker-writable directory. This includes builds started by `aspire sdk generate`, `aspire sdk dump`, and `aspire sdk export`. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a local attacker influencing a generated build through a shared temporary-directory ancestor while another user invokes the Aspire CLI. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120006 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Disclosure of an Aspire Dashboard authentication cookie to a linked service can allow an attacker-controlled container to replay the authenticated session and execute code as the host developer. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22092 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-201 (Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Hosting.AppHost](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting.AppHost) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Hosting](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario involves a Dashboard-authenticated AppHost workflow with an attacker-controlled container and a linked HTTPS YARP gateway. The affected hosting code is in `Aspire.Hosting`, a dependency of `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost`. `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` supplies the AppHost package implicitly unless the project overrides the default references. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a developer starting an Aspire AppHost, authenticating to its Dashboard, and following a resource link that routes to an attacker-controlled container. All released versions through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire components have been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the AppHost project's `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package reference to version 13.6.5 or later. If the project obtains this package implicitly through `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`, update that SDK reference to version 13.6.5 or later. Explicit package references or central version pins must also resolve `Aspire.Hosting` to version 13.6.5 or later. Restore dependencies, rebuild, and restart the AppHost after updating. Updating only the .NET runtime, .NET SDK, Aspire CLI, or standalone Dashboard does not replace the AppHost project's hosting dependencies. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-120006](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120006) ### Acknowledgements - samthewhitehat ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114155 - .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the .NET SDK's dotnet-watch component. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected SDK installations. A local attacker who can replace or modify a temporary solution file used by dotnet-watch can alter a subsequent build. The fix stores generated solution files in a private temporary directory and keeps each file open with read-only sharing while the build uses it. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/57040 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-367 - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Elevation of Privilege ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS. - **Architectures:** Linux: Arm, Arm64, x64; macOS: Arm64, x64 Windows is outside this advisory's affected scope when its temporary directory is private to the current user, as assumed by the implementation. Shared or insecurely configured Windows temporary directories are not covered by that assumption. ## Affected Packages The .NET SDK includes dotnet-watch and the Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch assembly. Each SDK feature band is a separate servicing line. Update an affected 10.0.3xx installation to the fixed 10.0.4xx SDK listed below. ### .NET SDK 10.0.3xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.3xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 10.0.4xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.4xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 11.0.1xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 11.0.1xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 ### Separately restored Aspire watch tool Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 This tool has its own copy of the watch implementation. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately restored tool. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Run `dotnet --version` from the directory where you run dotnet-watch to identify the selected SDK. Use `dotnet --info` and `dotnet --list-sdks` to check its installation path, OS, architecture, and other installed SDKs. Check the nearest applicable `global.json`, including its `version` and `rollForward` settings: installing a newer SDK does not necessarily change the SDK selected for a pinned project. See [.NET SDK selection](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/versions/selection). Review use of dotnet-watch against the affected intervals above. Membership in a listed feature band alone does not establish that a specific SDK version is vulnerable. For Aspire or other tooling that separately restores Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire, check the actual restored package version separately from the selected SDK. ### How do I fix the issue? The fixed SDK versions are 10.0.404 and 11.0.100, as applicable. Update each affected SDK installation and restart dotnet-watch. For SDKs installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio to a release that includes a fixed SDK. Updating only an application runtime does not replace SDK-bundled tools. Ensure that `global.json` and its SDK roll-forward policy select a fixed SDK, then rerun `dotnet --version` in the working directory to verify the selection. The SDK-bundled watch tool is installed beneath that selected SDK's `DotnetTools/dotnet-watch` directory. If Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire is restored separately, update its package reference or the consuming tool's version configuration to 10.0.404 or 11.0.100, as applicable, restore the tool, and restart the consuming process. An SDK update alone does not update that restored copy. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-114155](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114155) ### Acknowledgements - [Ky0toFu](https://x.com/ky0tofu) ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Each advisory below remains the authoritative source for its affected versions and remediation. The fixes and required actions differ by CVE; a runtime or SDK update does not replace every standalone package or repair every application. **Feedback:** [Use the shared .NET Runtime feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280). Please include the CVE number in your question. **Announcement:** [November 2026 .NET Runtime security updates](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/498).
